# cellspecR ![cellspecR logo](reference/figures/logo-with-name.png)

- [cellspecR](#cellspecr-)
  - [Installation](#installation)
  - [Quick start](#quick-start)
  - [What the package provides](#what-the-package-provides)
  - [Review an export](#review-an-export)
  - [Data and reproducibility](#data-and-reproducibility)
  - [Contributing and license](#contributing-and-license)
  - [Branding](#branding)

`cellspecR` defines the `cellspec` 1.0 table contract for segmented
cells from multiplexed tissue images. It reads tool exports, validates
structure and semantics, and writes an integrity checked directory for
downstream analysis.

> **Status: 1.1.1.9000 development.** Integrity corrections are listed
> in `NEWS.md`. The `cellspec` 1.0 specification and the package API are
> stable. Readers that
> [`cs_formats()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_formats.md)
> marks as experimental may still change with the export formats of
> their tools. cellspecR is not yet on CRAN.

## Installation

``` r

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("CTTIR/cellspecR")
```

## Quick start

``` r

x <- cs_example()
print(x)
#> <cellspec> spec 1.0.0
#>   cells     80 in 2 images (2 samples)
#>   features  19: 16 intensity, 2 shape, 1 other
#>   markers   4: DAPI, CD3e, Pan-Cytokeratin, FOXP3
#>   pixel     0.5 um/px
#>   adjacency none
#>   source    simulate 1.0.0 (cellspecR simulator 1.1.1.9000)
cs_validate(x)
#> <cellspec validation> 45 checks: 0 fail, 0 warn, 0 skip, 45 pass
#> pass 45 other checks

policy <- cs_signal_policy(
  marker = c("CD3e", "FOXP3"),
  compartment = c("cell", "nucleus"),
  statistic = "mean"
)
signal <- cs_signal_matrix(x, policy)
dim(signal$signal)
#> [1] 80  2

destination <- file.path(tempdir(), "cellspec-example")
cs_write(x, destination, overwrite = TRUE)
cs_verify(destination)
#>                        file
#> cells.parquet cells.parquet
#> cellspec.json cellspec.json
#> 1                      DONE
#>                                                                       expected
#> cells.parquet 67ca57b984c08b81087d62183e3602dac68637447b40f3a7bf0697bc98557994
#> cellspec.json 789a70c4bc699d8eb2196e50458a9965082d8437a775d7e5e3d384c7d95cd376
#> 1             8b9e0f45af4252aad714ceb2eaf05ed773de68d616703237b0d1489880577dba
#>                                                                       observed
#> cells.parquet 67ca57b984c08b81087d62183e3602dac68637447b40f3a7bf0697bc98557994
#> cellspec.json 789a70c4bc699d8eb2196e50458a9965082d8437a775d7e5e3d384c7d95cd376
#> 1             8b9e0f45af4252aad714ceb2eaf05ed773de68d616703237b0d1489880577dba
#>                 ok
#> cells.parquet TRUE
#> cellspec.json TRUE
#> 1             TRUE
y <- cs_read_cellspec(destination)
identical(cs_cells(x), cs_cells(y))
#> [1] TRUE
```

## What the package provides

- [`cs_read()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_read.md)
  and
  [`cs_detect_format()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_detect_format.md)
  for tool exports, plus
  [`cs_column_map()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_column_map.md)
  for explicit generic tables.
- [`cs_new()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_new.md),
  accessors, subsetting and compact print and summary methods.
- [`cs_validate()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_validate.md)
  and
  [`cs_feature_support()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_feature_support.md)
  for structural and signal quality checks.
- Parquet or exact text storage with a JSON sidecar, SHA-256 manifest
  and atomic staging through
  [`cs_write()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_write.md)
  and
  [`cs_read_cellspec()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_read_cellspec.md).
- Explicit signal policies, marker maps, object binding and tiled
  ownership.
- Optional conversion to `SpatialExperiment` and AnnData,
  quality-control plots and a local Shiny review app.

The package does not segment images, normalize signals, gate cells or
perform spatial statistics. It keeps the table contract and provenance
at the boundary between those tools.

## Review an export

``` r

shiny::runApp(cs_app(), host = "127.0.0.1")
```

Upload a CSV/TSV, gzip-compressed table or supported RDS export, choose
its format and pixel size where required, then select **Read**. Results
and downloads are cleared when inputs change or a read fails. Canonical
directories can be opened locally with
`cs_app(path = "path/to/cellspec-directory")`; a browser file upload
accepts one file, not a directory.

Canonical integrity checks include hidden files and refuse symbolic-link
members. Use a directory containing actual files for portable handover.
Checksums detect changes but do not authenticate who produced the data.
Writers recheck destination contents before replacement; coordinate
simultaneous writers externally because this is not a file-locking
protocol.

## Data and reproducibility

The bundled export in `inst/extdata/` is synthetic and contains no
patient data. Reader fixtures record their generator, header grammar and
SHA-256 in `tests/testthat/fixtures/README.md`. Examples do not access
the network.

## Contributing and license

Contributions follow the [CTTIR contributing
guide](https://github.com/CTTIR/.github/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md). The
package is released under the MIT license.

## Use of LLM tools

Where applicable, LLM tools were used for narrowly defined,
non-authorial tasks: copyediting, prose refinement, Markdown/LaTeX
formatting, boilerplate scaffolding (such as CI configurations and build
scripts), and code refactoring. Tools included [Chat
AI](https://kisski.gwdg.de/leistungen/2-02-llm-service/), the KISSKI
(GWDG) service, and self-hosted **Mistral Small (24B, Apache-2.0)**
served through a local **vLLM architecture** on an Ubuntu Linux
workstation with Intel processors and NVIDIA GPUs. Self-hosted use also
includes models that were further trained (fine-tuned) or weight-edited
in-house for specific tasks. All self-hosted models ran locally, with no
data sent to third parties.

All scientific claims, methodological choices, analyses, interpretations
and conclusions remain the authors’ own. Where applicable, LLM-generated
material must be reviewed and revised before inclusion, and references
must be verified against their DOI, arXiv ID or ISBN.

Local software setup: vLLM with Python/PyTorch, plus R and RStudio.

## Branding

Editable R sources and regeneration instructions are in
[tools/branding](https://github.com/CTTIR/cellspecR/tree/main/tools/branding).

# Package index

## Specification

- [`cs_spec_version()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_spec_version.md)
  : Version of the cellspec specification
- [`cs_vocabulary()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_vocabulary.md)
  : Columns and controlled vocabularies of the cellspec format

## Object

- [`cs_new()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_new.md)
  : Create a cellspec object
- [`cs_cells()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_accessors.md)
  [`cs_measurements()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_accessors.md)
  [`cs_dictionary()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_accessors.md)
  [`cs_images()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_accessors.md)
  [`cs_channels()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_accessors.md)
  [`cs_provenance()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_accessors.md)
  [`cs_adjacency()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_accessors.md)
  : Access the components of a cellspec object
- [`cs_features()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_features.md)
  [`cs_markers()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_features.md)
  : Select features and markers by their dictionary entries
- [`is_cellspec()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/is_cellspec.md)
  : Test for a cellspec object

## Validation

- [`cs_validate()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_validate.md)
  [`cs_assert_valid()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_validate.md)
  : Validate a cellspec object
- [`cs_feature_support()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_feature_support.md)
  : Summarise the signal support of features per image

## Readers and storage

- [`cs_formats()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_formats.md)
  : List the available cellspec readers
- [`cs_detect_format()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_detect_format.md)
  : Detect the generic table format
- [`cs_column_map()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_column_map.md)
  : Validate a table column map
- [`cs_read()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_read.md)
  : Read a delimited table into a cellspec object
- [`cs_read_cellspec()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_read_cellspec.md)
  : Read a canonical cellspec directory
- [`cs_verify()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_verify.md)
  : Verify a canonical cellspec directory
- [`cs_write()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_write.md)
  : Write a cellspec directory
- [`cs_bind()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_bind.md)
  : Combine cellspec objects from different images
- [`cs_merge_tiles()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_merge_tiles.md)
  : Merge tiled cellspec objects using centroid ownership
- [`cs_read_npy()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_read_npy.md)
  [`cs_read_npz()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_read_npy.md)
  [`cs_write_npy()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_read_npy.md)
  [`cs_write_npz()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_read_npy.md)
  **\[experimental\]** : Read and write NumPy array files

## Signals

- [`cs_signal_policy()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_signal_policy.md)
  : Create a signal selection policy
- [`cs_signal_matrix()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_signal_matrix.md)
  : Select one signal per cell and marker
- [`cs_marker_map()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_marker_map.md)
  : Create a marker-name mapping
- [`cs_read_signal_policy()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_read_signal_policy.md)
  : Read a signal policy from JSON or CSV
- [`cs_write_signal_policy()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_write_signal_policy.md)
  : Write a signal policy as JSON or CSV

## Interoperability and app

- [`cs_as_spe()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_as_spe.md)
  : Convert a cellspec object to SpatialExperiment
- [`cs_from_spe()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_from_spe.md)
  : Convert a SpatialExperiment back to cellspec
- [`cs_as_anndata()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_as_anndata.md)
  : Convert a cellspec object to AnnData
- [`cs_app()`](https://cttir.github.io/cellspecR/dev/reference/cs_app.md)
  **\[stable\]** : Create the cellspec review application
